_comment: Display metadata for chains on MAINNET: how the UI presents each chain -
accent color, name, logo, list order, family and native currency symbol.
The testnet deployment reads chainInfos.testnet.json; the file is picked by
the app.isMainnet setting.
This file is the source of truth - restyling or renaming a chain is an edit
here, no frontend rebuild and no redeploy. Edits are picked up on the next
request (the file is re-read whenever its mtime changes), so no restart
either.
"chain" is the id the rest of the API uses (see enabledChains in /settings)
and is read lowercase. Only "chain" and "color" are required; every other
field falls back to a UI default when it is omitted. A chain with no entry
at all takes its accent from unknownChain - and the UI's own default accent
when that is not set either.
"label" is the name shown for the chain, defaulting to the capitalized id.
"order" places it in every chain list the UI draws, lowest first; entries
without one sort last. "category" is the chain family - utxo, evm or svm -
and picks the audit page tab and the bridge network filter, defaulting to
evm. "symbol" is the native currency ticker and "apexFusion" marks an Apex
Fusion chain, which the bridge can filter on.
"icon" is the file name of a logo THIS API serves under /icons/chains/, so
"prime.svg" is loaded from <apiUrl>/icons/chains/prime.svg. Updating a logo
is an overwrite of that file - browsers revalidate hourly, so it appears
within the hour. Append a query to force it sooner ("prime.svg?v=2" is a
new URL to a browser and the same file to this API). A name with no file
behind it falls back to the UI's bundled unknown logo, as does a missing
entry.
"iconUrl" overrides "icon" with an absolute URL, for a logo hosted
somewhere else. It must point straight at an image: a github.com/<org>/
<repo>/blob/... link serves HTML and will not render - use the
raw.githubusercontent.com form instead, and note that GitHub caches for
only 5 minutes even for a commit-pinned URL.
Which chains the bridge serves stays in enabledChains, but the UI only
draws a chain it finds here, so an entry is also what makes an enabled
chain visible. An entry for a chain this deployment does not serve is
simply unused.
